text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the information. Since you are a 5-year-old boy presenting for a well-child visit with new-onset hypertension, we need to investigate potential secondary causes. Do you have any abdominal pain, swelling in your legs, or changes in your urine like foaming or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that crucial detail. Is there any difference in the pulse or blood pressure between your arms and legs, or have you noticed any swelling in one side of your face or neck?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Born full term with an uneventful neonatal period. Social history: Patient attends kindergarten. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco smoke.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta.

Based on your history of hypertension isolated to the right upper extremity, combined with the lack of symptoms in the lower extremities, this is highly suggestive of a narrowing in the aorta. I need to confirm the physical findings and rule out other structural issues before finalizing the treatment plan.
